purpose: Score a work ABOVE the narrative-decision audit's 25,000-word ceiling by deterministic segmentation (chapter/scene/blank-line/paragraph tiers, greedy packing) plus per-segment scoring with the unchanged base audit. M1 emits per-segment raw responses only: every work-level aggregate is suppressed as provisional_unvalidated until a validation receipt exists (spec 77 M2). Not a provenance verdict; reducing per-segment values to a work-level scalar is derivable but outside the claim license.
use_when: Target is long-form fiction ABOVE 25,000 words (novels)
You want per-segment narrative-decision distributions across a book
Calibration segment emission for the spec 77/78 agreement studies
do_not_use_when: Target is within the base audit's 2,000-25,000 word range (use narrative_decision_audit)
You want a licensed work-level aggregate (none exists until M2's receipt)
You want an AI/human provenance verdict (never licensed by this surface)

compute.cost_note: Per-segment judge multiplier dominates: a novel at the default 5,000-word target is roughly 20-80 segments, i.e. 20-80 judge calls per audit (vs 1 for the base audit). Free with a precomputed per-segment manifest (keyed by segment content hash), which is also the only licensable path today. Content-hash+judge-identity cache makes reruns cheap.
